## 0. Useful conclusion and its limit
A single PERMANENT onsite gauge can protect the same continuously running native controllers while a finite local program register is repeatedly driven toward different absolute transversal frames. Native controllers need not become idle, be reset, or have their forest frame physically inverted between commands. Neither local dimension nor interaction support grows with command depth. After a fixed settling time, one ordinary product DATA decoder reads the actual cumulative logical frame, up to an exponentially small channel error depending on total elapsed physical time, not a sum of separate per-command restart errors.

The scope is a FIXED number b of colocated identical CSS blocks and a fixed finite group Gamma of onsite gates whose uniform transversal actions preserve their product code. For an explicit noncommuting example, b=2 and Gamma=GL(2,F_2), the six two-bit permutation matrices generated by forward and reverse CNOT. These are exact unitary representatives, with no projective-phase convention. This does NOT supply arbitrary partner changes across an unbounded number of blocks. Uniform finite-group instruction streams are classically compressible to a final group element; this construction does not give a computational speedup over an equally informed scheduled route.

source_excerpts.text:
## 2. A finite register which can retire every stale intermediate
Let m=|Gamma|. At each column introduce m^2 orthonormal labels

    r_g (g in Gamma),
    e_(a,b) (a,b in Gamma, a!=b).

Here the symbol b in e_(a,b) is a group label, not the block count. Define the label-to-frame map w(r_g)=g and w(e_(a,b))=b, and the PERMANENT onsite unitary

    G_i=sum_q u_(w(q)),i tensor |q><q|,
    G=product_i G_i.

For a commanded ABSOLUTE target v in Gamma, the program-frame Hamiltonian and always-on resets are

    H_v=Omega sum_(g!=v) (|e_(g,v)><r_g|+|r_g><e_(g,v)|),
    J_(a,b)=sqrt(kappa)|r_b><e_(a,b)|,  a!=b.

Omega,kappa>0 are fixed. The J_(a,b) are SEPARATE label-resolved Lindblad channels. They are not coherently summed into one jump per target b: such a different reservoir can create stale dark superpositions and is not this model. The Hamiltonian is a direct sum of disjoint 2x2 edges, not a star with dark ready superpositions. ALL intermediate resets remain on under every command. In particular an old e_(a,b), b!=v, first decays to r_b, then follows the current b->v pair. No new labels recursively indexed by old intermediate labels are needed.

The actual physical nominal generator at time t is EXACTLY

    L_phys,nom(t)=Ad_G [L_mem + sum_i L_prog,i(t)] Ad_Gdagger.

The native memory part is time-independent. During a settled command, L_prog,i is the preceding H_v/J generator. Thus the physical coherent command edge is

    Omega[u_v u_g^dagger tensor |e_(g,v)><r_g| + h.c.],

an allowed onsite joint Hamiltonian. Every physical J_(a,b) remains CLOCK-ONLY because source and target have the SAME frame b. This is the actual finite handoff operation; it does not reset native hub/lock/workspace registers and does not apply F_mem^{-1}.

Commands are ABSOLUTE frames. To represent requested relative gates a_1,...,a_K, an external classical controller computes v_j=a_j...a_1 and commands v_j. Commanding a_j alone would overwrite the target, NOT apply a_j to the previous logical frame. This distinction is part of the interface.

## 3. Exact absorption Gramian, including arbitrary stale coherences
Fix v and let Q_v=I-|r_v><r_v|. The active pairs are (r_g,e_(g,v)), g!=v. Every remaining intermediate e_(a,b), b!=v, jumps into r_b and then follows the active b-to-v pair. There are m-1 active pairs and (m-1)^2 stale intermediates.

I independently derived the following exact solution, which agrees with the governing construction. On each active pair put

    R2=[[2/kappa+kappa/(4 Omega^2), -i/(2 Omega)],
        [i/(2 Omega),              2/kappa]].

On each stale intermediate put D=3/kappa+kappa/(4 Omega^2); on r_v put zero. All other entries vanish. The active-pair equation is the actual coherent two-state killed equation. The stale diagonal equation is

    kappa(R2)_(r,r)-kappa D=-1.

Separate jumps produce no off-diagonal gain terms. Consequently the FULL adjoint obeys

    L_prog,v* R_v=-Q_v

on the entire register, not only on populations. R2 is positive, with determinant 4/kappa^2+1/(4 Omega^2)>0, and D>lambda_max(R2). Thus for m>=2,

    Rmax=D, a=lambda_min(R2)/D>0, r=1/D,
    A_v=R_v/D,
    aQ_v<=A_v<=Q_v,   L_prog,v*A_v=-rQ_v<=-rA_v.

The constants are uniform in v and even independent of m. Positivity makes the estimate valid for arbitrary stale ready/intermediate coherences, including correlations with DATA, native controllers, a common bath and a reference. No instantaneous dephasing or classical initial program distribution is assumed. It also proves uniqueness of the absorbing state: any stationary positive state has zero Q_v population.

The trivial m=1 case needs no clock and is outside the displayed nontrivial formula; it does not affect the concrete six-element construction.
